    # =========================================================================
# web/application_model.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The cache/facade of the business layer (the equivalent of the class
# [ApplicationModel] in previous versions of the application): the
# lists of doctors and clients are read once at startup, then
# retrieved from memory.
#
# These lists can be CHANGER (the ADMIN adds, modifies, or deletes
# doctors and clients): every write operation therefore goes through this facade,
# which then updates the relevant list immediately afterward. This is the whole point of a
# entry point UNIQUE to the business layer: the rule “update =>
# cache reload” is implemented only here.
#
# A single object for the entire application, used by
# processed by EN PARALLÈLE, across multiple threads. Therefore, we never modify
# a list in place: the entire list is REMPLACE replaced with a new one. In Python,
# assigning a value to an attribute is atomic: a thread reading the list sees
# either the old or the new one, never a list that’s halfway constructed.
# =========================================================================
from datetime import date

from rdvmedecins.domain.agenda import AgendaMedecinJour
from rdvmedecins.entities import Client, Creneau, Medecin, Rv
from rdvmedecins.metier.donnees import DonneesPersonne
from rdvmedecins.metier.metier import Metier


# same contract as the business layer (Metier)
class ApplicationModel:

    def __init__(self, metier: Metier):
        self._metier = metier
         # Initial loading of both lists upon application startup.
         # A read error (database inaccessible...) is not caught:
         # It shuts down the server rather than letting it start "from scratch"
        self._medecins: list[Medecin] = []
        self._clients: list[Client] = []
        self._recharger_medecins()
        self._recharger_clients()

    def _recharger_medecins(self):
        self._medecins = list(self._metier.get_all_medecins())

    def _recharger_clients(self):
        self._clients = list(self._metier.get_all_clients())

     # ------------------------------------------------ reads from the cache

    def get_all_medecins(self) -> list[Medecin]:
        return self._medecins

    def get_all_clients(self) -> list[Client]:
        return self._clients

     # the doctor whose user account is [id_user]—is used for preselection,
     # for a logged-in doctor, their own calendar
    def get_medecin_by_user_id(self, id_user: int) -> Medecin | None:
        return next((m for m in self._medecins if m.id_user == id_user), None)

     # ------------------------------------------------ simple delegations

    def get_all_creneaux(self, id_medecin: int) -> list[Creneau]:
        return self._metier.get_all_creneaux(id_medecin)

    def get_rv_medecin_jour(self, id_medecin: int, jour: date) -> list[Rv]:
        return self._metier.get_rv_medecin_jour(id_medecin, jour)

    def get_client_by_id(self, id: int) -> Client | None:
        return self._metier.get_client_by_id(id)

    def get_medecin_by_id(self, id: int) -> Medecin | None:
        return self._metier.get_medecin_by_id(id)

    def get_rv_by_id(self, id: int) -> Rv | None:
        return self._metier.get_rv_by_id(id)

    def get_creneau_by_id(self, id: int) -> Creneau | None:
        return self._metier.get_creneau_by_id(id)

    def get_agenda_medecin_jour(self, id_medecin: int, jour: date) -> AgendaMedecinJour | None:
        return self._metier.get_agenda_medecin_jour(id_medecin, jour)

     # no cache here: the most recent data is what counts (a patient
     # who has just modified or deleted their account)
    def get_client_by_user_id(self, id_user: int) -> Client | None:
        return self._metier.get_client_by_user_id(id_user)

    def get_rv_a_venir_client(self, id_client: int) -> list[Rv]:
        return self._metier.get_rv_a_venir_client(id_client)

    def ajouter_rv(self, jour: date, creneau: Creneau, client: Client) -> Rv:
        return self._metier.ajouter_rv(jour, creneau, client)

    def supprimer_rv(self, rv: Rv) -> None:
        self._metier.supprimer_rv(rv)

     # ------------------------------------------------ entries => reload

    def ajouter_medecin(self, donnees: DonneesPersonne) -> Medecin:
        medecin = self._metier.ajouter_medecin(donnees)
        self._recharger_medecins()
        return medecin

    def modifier_medecin(self, id: int, donnees: DonneesPersonne) -> Medecin:
        medecin = self._metier.modifier_medecin(id, donnees)
        self._recharger_medecins()
        return medecin

    def supprimer_medecin(self, id: int) -> None:
        self._metier.supprimer_medecin(id)
        self._recharger_medecins()

    def ajouter_client(self, donnees: DonneesPersonne) -> Client:
        client = self._metier.ajouter_client(donnees)
        self._recharger_clients()
        return client

    def modifier_client(self, id: int, donnees: DonneesPersonne) -> Client:
        client = self._metier.modifier_client(id, donnees)
        self._recharger_clients()
        return client

    def supprimer_client(self, id: int) -> None:
        self._metier.supprimer_client(id)
        self._recharger_clients()

    The web layer cache and its interface to the business layer:

    • lines 32–40: the lists of doctors and patients are read once, at startup. They are used every time the calendar is displayed (the drop-down list of doctors, the list of patients): keeping them in memory avoids two SQL requests per page. A read error is not caught: it causes the application to crash at startup (see “Common Problems”);
    • lines 50–59: data retrieved from the cache. [get_medecin_by_user_id] identifies the logged-in doctor to preselect their own calendar;
    • lines 63–96: the other read operations, and the appointments, are simply relayed to the business layer. [get_client_by_user_id] does not use the cache: a patient who has just modified or deleted their account must see the most recent data;
    • lines 100–126: Each update to doctors or clients refreshes the relevant list. This is the benefit of a single entry point to the business layer: the rule “update, then refresh the cache” is implemented only here.

    This unique object is used by requests processed in parallel across multiple threads: therefore, a list is never modified in place (by [append] or [remove]); instead, it is replaced entirely with a new one. In [Python], assigning an attribute is atomic: a thread reading the list sees either the old or the new version, never a partially constructed list. Therefore, no lock is needed.

    [ApplicationModel] adheres to the [Metier] contract (it has the same methods as [MetierService]): for the controllers, it is the business layer. We could remove the cache without touching the controllers by directly placing [MetierService] inside [app.extensions].

# web/validation.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What’s needed for a rejected form: the errors in
# field-by-field, and the fields to be highlighted in red.
# =========================================================================
from flask_wtf import FlaskForm

from rdvmedecins.models.modeles_vues import EtatFormulaire, Message


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# the validated form (see forms/formulaires.py) -> the dictionary
# field -> message key, keeping only the first message from each
# field: { "name": "ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED", ... }
#
# Our messages are translation keys ("ERRORS...."). A message that
# WTForms wrote himself (in English) is replaced by the key
# ERRORS.INVALID_FORM.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def erreurs_de(form: FlaskForm) -> dict[str, str]:
    erreurs = {}
    for champ, messages in form.errors.items():
        message = str(messages[0])
        erreurs[champ] = message if message.startswith("ERRORS.") else "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM"
    return erreurs


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# the form fields affected by each business "data entry" error
# (a duplicate): they are highlighted in red, with the message at the bottom of the page
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER = {
    "ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN": ["login"],
    "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS": ["prenom", "nom"],
    "ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS": ["prenom", "nom"],
}


# the status of a form to be (re)displayed: a message below each field
# rejected by validation (errors), and the fields to be highlighted in red,
# these and any others (autres_champs)
def etat(erreurs: dict[str, str], autres_champs: list[str] | None = None) -> EtatFormulaire:
    return EtatFormulaire(dict(erreurs), set(erreurs) | set(autres_champs or []))


# LE page error message, displayed at the bottom of the page: [erreur] if
# there is one, otherwise "The form contains errors." if there are
# field errors, otherwise nothing
def message_page(erreurs: dict[str, str], erreur: Message | None) -> Message | None:
    if erreur is not None:
        return erreur
    return Message("ERRORS.INVALID_FORM") if erreurs else None

    What is needed to redisplay a rejected form:

    • lines 21–26: the errors from a [WTForms] form (example 19), in the form of a “field → message key” dictionary, keeping only the first message for each field. The messages from our validators are translation keys ([ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED], see [forms/formulaires.py]); a message that [WTForms] would have generated itself, in English, is replaced by a generic key;
    • lines 33–36: Some business-logic errors pertain to specific fields—such as a username that’s already taken or a name with the same spelling. Their error messages appear at the bottom of the page, but the affected fields are highlighted in red so the user can immediately see what to correct (see the screenshot of the name with the same spelling above);
    • lines 43–44: the state of a form to be redisplayed: the messages below the fields, and all fields to be highlighted in red. [set(erreurs)] is the set of keys in the dictionary; the operator [|] performs a union of two sets;
    • lines 50–53: the general footer message.

    # =========================================================================
# web/outils.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Small utility functions in the web layer:
#    - labels: "Ms. Alice DURAND";
#    - dates: "yyyy-mm-dd", times "8:05", days "Wednesday, September 23, 2026";
#    - input: reading a positive integer sent by the browser;
#    - user: the logged-in user and their patient (Client entity).
# =========================================================================
import re
from datetime import date, datetime

from babel.dates import format_date
from flask import g

from rdvmedecins.auth.securite import SessionInvalide
from rdvmedecins.auth.utilisateur import UtilisateurConnecte
from rdvmedecins.entities import Client, Creneau, Personne

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- labels


# "Ms. Alice DURAND"
def libelle(p: Personne) -> str:
    return f"{p.titre} {p.prenom} {p.nom}"


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- dates

# the date format in URL and in the <input type="date"> field
FORMAT_ISO = re.compile(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}")


# the date, if [texte] is a valid date in the yyyy-mm-dd format; None otherwise.
# strptime checks that the date exists: "2026-02-30" is rejected
def date_valide(texte: str | None) -> date | None:
    if texte is None or not FORMAT_ISO.fullmatch(texte):
        return None
    try:
        return datetime.strptime(texte, "%Y-%m-%d").date()
    except ValueError:
        return None


def iso(jour: date) -> str:
    return jour.isoformat()


# "8:05" rather than "8:5"
def formater_heure(h: int, m: int) -> str:
    return f"{h}:{m:02d}"


def horaire(c: Creneau) -> str:
    return f"{formater_heure(c.hdebut, c.mdebut)} - {formater_heure(c.hfin, c.mfin)}"


# "Wednesday, September 23, 2026" / "Wednesday 23 September 2026," depending on the
# language of the request (g.langue). The Babel format: EEEE the day of the
# the week spelled out, d the day, MMMM the month spelled out, y the year
def formater_jour(jour: date) -> str:
    return format_date(jour, "EEEE d MMMM y", locale=g.langue)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- input


# "3" -> 3; "", "abc", "-2", "+2", None -> None
def entier_positif(valeur: str | None) -> int | None:
    if valeur is None or not re.fullmatch(r"\d{1,9}", valeur):
        return None
    n = int(valeur)
    return n if n > 0 else None


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- user


# the logged-in user (see auth/securite.py). Protected actions are
# are called only if it exists; as a precaution, its absence is treated
# as an expired session.
def utilisateur() -> UtilisateurConnecte:
    if g.utilisateur is None:
        raise SessionInvalide()
    return g.utilisateur


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# The patient (Client entity) that corresponds to the logged-in user.
#
# The token JWT contains only the ID of COMPTE (users.id). For a role
# For USER, the corresponding client is identified using the clients.user column.
#
# If there is no match, it means the account was deleted since the
# login, even though its token is still valid: it is treated as a
# expired session (see SessionInvalide).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def patient_connecte(application) -> Client:
    patient = application.get_client_by_user_id(utilisateur().user_id)
    if patient is None:
        raise SessionInvalide()
    return patient

    Utility functions used by multiple controllers:

    • line 24: a person’s title, “Ms. Alice DURAND”;
    • lines 31–42: parsing a date in the [aaaa-mm-jj] format, which is the same as that used for the URL entries in the calendar ([jour=2026-09-26]) and the [<input type="date">] field. The regular expression checks the format ([fullmatch]: the entire string must match), while [strptime] checks for the existence of the date. An invalid date results in [None]: the action determines the outcome;
    • lines 50–51: the format [02d] outputs a two-digit integer, padded with zeros: [8:05];
    • lines 61–62: a date written out in full, in the language of the query, with [Babel] (example 16). The format is explicitly specified here: [EEEE], the day of the week spelled out; [d], the day; [MMMM], the month spelled out; [y], the year;
    • lines 69–73: reading an identifier sent by the browser (a parameter of URL, a hidden field). [\d{1,9}]: one to nine digits, which excludes characters, spaces, and numbers too large for a [INT] column. Anything coming from the browser may have been modified: it must be verified before use;
    • lines 82–85: the logged-in user; its absence (which should not occur in a protected action) is treated as an expired session;
    • lines 98–102: the patient (the entity [Client]) corresponding to the logged-in user. The token contains only the account ID: the patient is identified by the [clients.user] column. If it does not exist, it means the account has been deleted since the user logged in.

# forms/regles.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The data entry rules common to "person" forms and FILTRES
# and WTForms (see Example 19): functions that transform the value
# received after validation.
# =========================================================================
TITRES = ("Mr", "Mme", "Melle")

# login: lowercase letters, numbers, period, hyphen, underscore—30 characters maximum
FORMAT_LOGIN = r"^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$"

# minimum password length CHOISI for a patient
MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN = 6


# "   dupont " -> "dupont"; "    " -> None
def nettoyer(valeur):
    if not isinstance(valeur, str):
        return valeur
    return valeur.strip() or None


# "   Dupont " -> "dupont": a username is always in lowercase
def login(valeur):
    valeur = nettoyer(valeur)
    return valeur.lower() if isinstance(valeur, str) else valeur


# an empty field -> None; for a password, spaces are not removed PAS
# spaces (they may be part of the password)
def vide_en_none(valeur):
    return valeur if valeur else None


# the hidden field [version]: an integer, or None if it is missing or empty.
# Text that is not a number: a ValueError, which WTForms converts
# into a field error, with this message (a translation key)
def version(valeur):
    if valeur in (None, ""):
        return None
    try:
        return int(valeur)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        raise ValueError("ERRORS.INVALID_FORM")

    Input rules common to all forms, and the [WTForms] filters (example 19):

    • lines 8–14: allowed titles, the format of a username (lowercase letters, numbers, period, hyphen, underscore, up to 30 characters), and the minimum length of a password chosen by a patient;
    • Lines 18–21: The spaces surrounding an entry are removed; an empty entry becomes [None]. [a or b] is equivalent to [b] if [a] is “false” (in this case, an empty string);
    • lines 25–27: a username is always in lowercase;
    • lines 32–33: for a password, spaces are not removed, as they may be part of the password;
    • lines 39–45: the hidden version field (the optimistic lock): an integer, or [None]. A filter that returns a value like [ValueError] triggers a field error, with the error message matching that of the exception: a browser that submits anything other than a number would receive the “invalid form” error.

    # =========================================================================
# forms/formulaires.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The fields in the "person" forms and their constraints (see examples
# 19 and 28). Three forms share the same identity fields
# (title, first name, last name):
#
#    ChampsPersonn               e title, first name, last name
#     ├─ FormulairePerson       ne + login / password FACULTATIFS, version
#                                   │ (ADMIN adds or modifies a doctor/client)
#     ├─ FormulaireInscripti    on + login / password / confirmation OBLIGATOIRES
#                                   │ (a patient creates an account)
#     └─ FormulaireMonComp      te + username, optional new password,
#                                    ACTUEL password required, version
#                                    (a patient modifies their account)
#
# A class WTForms that inherits from another class also inherits its fields.
#
# LIAISON: FormulairePersonne() reads the fields with the same name from the
# current POST query (request.form), and applies its filters to them
# (unnecessary spaces removed, login in lowercase...).
# VALIDATION: form.validate() then checks the constraints of each
# field, in order; the first one that fails stores its message in
# form.<field>.errors. These messages are translation strings (see i18n/*.json).
#
# Forms are used here solely to read and validate user input: the views
# generate their own <input> tags based on the view templates
# (see models/modeles_vues.py).
# =========================================================================
from flask_wtf import FlaskForm
from wtforms import PasswordField, StringField
from wtforms.validators import AnyOf, DataRequired, InputRequired, Length, Optional, Regexp

from rdvmedecins.forms import regles


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ common base
class ChampsPersonne(FlaskForm):

    titre = StringField(validators=[AnyOf(regles.TITRES, message="ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE")])

     # maximum lengths = those of the columns in SQL (VARCHAR(20)).
     # DataRequired stops field validation if the field is empty: the message
     # from Length is therefore never added to this one
    prenom = StringField(filters=[regles.nettoyer], validators=[
        DataRequired("ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_REQUIRED"),
        Length(max=20, message="ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_TOO_LONG")])

    nom = StringField(filters=[regles.nettoyer], validators=[
        DataRequired("ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED"),
        Length(max=20, message="ERRORS.LASTNAME_TOO_LONG")])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ ADMIN
class FormulairePersonne(ChampsPersonne):

     # optional (see business/donnees.py): "Optional" stops validation of a
     # empty field, without an error
    login = StringField(filters=[regles.login], validators=[
        Optional(), Regexp(regles.FORMAT_LOGIN, message="ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")])

     # optional; maximum 72 characters (if longer, bcrypt ignores the rest)
    password = PasswordField(filters=[regles.vide_en_none], validators=[
        Optional(strip_whitespace=False), Length(max=72, message="ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")])

     # hidden field in the edit form (optimistic lock)
    version = StringField(filters=[regles.version])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ patient registration
class FormulaireInscription(ChampsPersonne):

     # InputRequired: the entry must not be empty
    login = StringField(filters=[regles.login], validators=[
        InputRequired("ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED"),
        Regexp(regles.FORMAT_LOGIN, message="ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")])

     # Two "Length" constraints, each with its own message
    password = PasswordField(filters=[regles.vide_en_none], validators=[
        InputRequired("ERRORS.PASSWORD_REQUIRED"),
        Length(min=regles.MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN, message="ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT"),
        Length(max=72, message="ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")])

    confirmation = PasswordField(filters=[regles.vide_en_none], validators=[
        InputRequired("ERRORS.CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED")])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ "Manage My Account"
class FormulaireMonCompte(ChampsPersonne):

    login = StringField(filters=[regles.login], validators=[
        InputRequired("ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED"),
        Regexp(regles.FORMAT_LOGIN, message="ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")])

     # optional: empty = password unchanged
    password = PasswordField(filters=[regles.vide_en_none], validators=[
        Optional(strip_whitespace=False),
        Length(min=regles.MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN, message="ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT"),
        Length(max=72, message="ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")])

    confirmation = PasswordField(filters=[regles.vide_en_none])

     # the password ACTUEL, required for any account changes
    mot_de_passe_actuel = PasswordField(filters=[regles.vide_en_none], validators=[
        InputRequired("ERRORS.CURRENT_PASSWORD_REQUIRED")])

    version = StringField(filters=[regles.version])
    • Lines 38–51: the fields common to all three forms: title, first name, last name. The validator messages are translation keys: the view will translate them into the page’s language. The [AnyOf] validator accepts a value from a list. The maximum lengths are those of the SQL columns: a longer entry would be rejected by the database;
    • lines 55–67: the administrator form: a login and an optional password (the [Optional] validator stops validating an empty field without reporting an error; [strip_whitespace=False]: a password consisting of spaces is not considered empty), and the version;
    • lines 71–85: the patient registration form: username, password, and confirmation are required. Two validators, [Length], each with its own message: too short, too long;
    • lines 89–107: “Manage My Account”: an optional new password, and the current password, which is required for any changes.

    A class named [WTForms], which inherits from another class, inherits its fields: the three forms share the fields of [ChampsPersonne]. The comparison of the password and its confirmation is not handled by the [EqualTo] validator (Example 19), but is performed by the action, which thus selects the message and the relevant field.

    Note that these forms are used only to read and validate user input: the views do not call the [WTForms] fields to render them (Example 18); instead, they write their own [<input>] tags based on the view templates. This approach keeps the views identical across all three forms and gives the action complete control over what is displayed (never a password, for example). This is also the approach used in previous versions of the application.

    # =========================================================================
# models/modeles_vues.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# "View models": what each action passes to its
# view, under the name [modele]. These are dataclasses: objects constructed
# once by the action, which the view simply reads
# ({{ modele.agenda.lignes }}...).
#
# Rule followed by all pages: no logic in the views. The
# actions prepare formatted data DÉJÀ ("Ms. Marie
# PELISSIER", "8:00 - 8:20", selectionne = True...) and already filtered according to
# the user’s role; the views simply place them in the HTML.
#
# Each page template has two fields, read by the template (templates/layout.html):
# titre_page, the page title key, and error, LE error message from
# the page, displayed at the bottom of the page (None: no error).
# =========================================================================
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from rdvmedecins.auth.captcha import Captcha
from rdvmedecins.forms import regles


# a message to be translated: its key and its parameters
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Message:
    cle: str
    parametres: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)


# an option from a drop-down list (doctor, patient)
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OptionVue:
    id: int
    libelle: str
    selectionne: bool


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ login
@dataclass
class LoginModele:
    titre_page: str
    erreur: Message | None
    login: str
    captcha: Captcha


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ calendar
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LigneAgendaVue:
    id_creneau: int
    horaire: str  # "8:00 - 8:20"
    libre: bool
    patient: str | None  # display name for a booked slot; None = “Reserved”
    moi: bool  # the logged-in patient’s appointment
    reservable: bool  # Display the "Book" button?
    url_reserver: str
    id_rv: int | None  # filled in only if the "Cancel" button is displayed


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AgendaVue:
    medecin: str
    jour: str
    lignes: list[LigneAgendaVue]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReservationVue:
    id_creneau: int
    horaire: str
    clients: list[OptionVue]  # ADMIN / DOCTOR: patients to choose from
    patient: str | None  # USER: the patient is the patient themselves


@dataclass
class AgendaModele:
    titre_page: str
    erreur: Message | None
    medecins: list[OptionVue]
    id_medecin: int | None
    jour: str  # "yyyy-mm-dd"
    agenda: AgendaVue | None
    reservation: ReservationVue | None
    url_retour: str  # the displayed calendar, without a booking window
     # Patient who already has an upcoming appointment: the explanatory message
     # why there is no “Book” button
    info: str | None


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ "Person" forms

# the values displayed in the form fields (never the password)
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ValeursPersonne:
    titre: str = "Mr"
    prenom: str = ""
    nom: str = ""
    login: str = ""
    version: int | None = None


# the status of a rejected form: the message displayed SOUS for each field
# (field -> message key), and the fields to be highlighted in red (class
# Bootstrap is-invalid): those with a message, plus any others
# (duplicate first name + last name, username already taken...)
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EtatFormulaire:
    erreurs: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    champs_invalides: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)

    def erreur_de(self, champ: str) -> str | None:
        return self.erreurs.get(champ)

    def classe_invalide(self, champ: str) -> str:
        return "is-invalid" if champ in self.champs_invalides else ""


# an option from the list of titles
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OptionTitre:
    valeur: str
    selectionne: bool


# what the common fragment champs_personne.html uses (title, first name, last name):
# a base class from which the three form templates inherit
@dataclass
class FormulaireVue:
    titre_page: str
    erreur: Message | None
    valeurs: ValeursPersonne
    etat: EtatFormulaire

     # a property: reads like an attribute (modele.titres), but is calculated
    @property
    def titres(self) -> list[OptionTitre]:
        return [OptionTitre(t, t == self.valeurs.titre) for t in regles.TITRES]

    @property
    def mot_de_passe_min(self) -> int:
        return regles.MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN


@dataclass
class FormulairePersonneModele(FormulaireVue):
    creation: bool  # True: addition; False: modification
    action: str  # URL from POST
    url_liste: str


@dataclass
class InscriptionModele(FormulaireVue):
    pass


@dataclass
class MonCompteModele(FormulaireVue):
    pass


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ lists of doctors / clients

# translation keys specific to each person type
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ClesPersonnes:
    titre: str  # "Doctors"
    ajouter: str  # "Add a doctor"
    modifier: str  # "Edit a doctor"
    vide: str  # "No doctors."
    confirmer_suppression: str  # "Delete this doctor and their account?"
    ajoute: str  # "The doctor {name} has been added (login: {login})."
    modifie: str
    supprime: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PersonneVue:
    titre: str
    prenom: str
    nom: str
    login: str
    url_modifier: str
    url_supprimer: str


@dataclass
class ListePersonnesModele:
    titre_page: str
    erreur: Message | None
    cles: ClesPersonnes
    url_ajouter: str
    personnes: list[PersonneVue]


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ patient area
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RendezVousVue:
    id: int
    jour: str
    horaire: str
    medecin: str
    url_agenda: str


@dataclass
class EspaceModele:
    titre_page: str
    erreur: Message | None
    patient: str
    rendez_vous: list[RendezVousVue]


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ error page
@dataclass
class ErreurModele:
    titre_page: str
    erreur: Message | None
    code: int
    message: str

    View models (*view models*): what each action passes to its view, under the name [modele]. The rule followed by all pages: no logic in the views. Actions prepare data that is already formatted (“Ms. Marie PELISSIER,” “8:00 – 8:20”) and already filtered according to the user’s role; views simply place this data into the HTML.

    • lines 26–28: a message to be translated: a key and its parameters. [field(default_factory=dict)]: the default value is a new, empty dictionary for each object. You cannot write [= {}]: this dictionary would be created only once and shared by all objects;
    • lines 33–36: an option from a drop-down list;
    • lines 41–45: the login page template. Each page template has two fields read by the template: [titre_page], the page title key, and [erreur], the error message displayed at the bottom of the page;
    • lines 50–58: a row in the calendar, already populated for the logged-in user: [patient] is equivalent to [None] for a time slot occupied by another patient, when the user is a patient (the view will display “Reserved”) ; [reservable] indicates whether to display the “Book” button; [id_rv] is populated only if the “Cancel” button is to be displayed. All these decisions are made by the action;
    • lines 69–73: the booking window: the list of patients for an administrator or doctor, the patient’s name for a patient;
    • lines 77–88: the calendar page template;
    • lines 108–116: the state of a rejected form, with two methods called by the views: the message for a field, and the class CSS that highlights it in red;
    • lines 129–142: the base class for the three form templates, used by the common fragment [champs_personne.html]. Its two properties calculate the list of titles (including the selected title) and the minimum length of a password;
    • Lines 146–158: The three form templates inherit from [FormulaireVue]. A [dataclass] that inherits from another adds its fields to those of its parent class;
    • lines 166–174: translation keys specific to doctors or clients: the same view displays both lists;
    • lines 198–211: the patient area;
    • lines 216–220: the error page.

    11.16. The Web Layer: Controllers

    The [controllers] folder contains one blueprint per part of the application (the login controller, [controllers/auth.py], was introduced with authentication):

    Blueprint
    Addresses
    [langue]
    [GET /langue/<code>]
    [agenda]
    [GET /agenda], [POST /agenda/reserver], [POST /agenda/annuler]
    [medecins], [clients]
    [/medecins/...], [/clients/...]: list, add, edit, delete
    [inscription]
    [POST /inscription/acces], [GET], and [POST /inscription]
    [espace]
    [/mon-espace], [/mon-espace/annuler], [/mon-compte], [/mon-compte/supprimer]

    All actions follow the same pattern: read and validate the request, call the business layer (via [ApplicationModel]), build the view model; or, for an action such as POST, post a flash message and redirect (flow PRG, example 20).

    # =========================================================================
# controllers/langue.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /language/fr, GET /language/en: the two buttons FR / EN on the
# navigation bar. Public road: You should be able to change the language before
# logging in.
#
# The selection is stored in a cookie: for each subsequent request, the
# function fixer_langue (see rdvmedecins/__init__.py) reads it and sets the
# language of the request (g.langue). You are then redirected back to the page you came from.
# =========================================================================
from datetime import timedelta
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from flask import Blueprint, abort, current_app, redirect, request

from rdvmedecins.auth.securite import publique
from rdvmedecins.web.traducteur import COOKIE_LANGUE, LANGUES

langue = Blueprint("langue", __name__)


@langue.get("/langue/<code>")
@publique
def changer(code: str):
    if code not in LANGUES:
        abort(404)  # -> 404 error page (see web/erreurs.py)
    reponse = redirect(page_d_origine())
    reponse.set_cookie(COOKIE_LANGUE, code, max_age=timedelta(days=365), path="/",
                       httponly=True, samesite="Lax", secure=current_app.config["COOKIE_SECURE"])
    return reponse


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# the previous page, based on the "Referer" header HTTP sent by the
# browser. We only keep the path (/agenda?...): redirect to
# a complete address provided by the request would allow us to send
# the user to another site (a vulnerability known as an “open redirect”).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def page_d_origine() -> str:
    referer = request.headers.get("Referer")
    if not referer:
        return "/"
    url = urlsplit(referer)
    chemin = url.path
     # "//site.com/..." would be interpreted by the browser as an address
     # to a AUTRE site: also rejected
    if not url.scheme or not chemin.startswith("/") or chemin.startswith("//") \
            or chemin.startswith("/langue/"):
        return "/"
    return f"{chemin}?{url.query}" if url.query else chemin

    The language selection from Example 22, with two additional precautions in [page_d_origine] (lines 40–51): a [Referer] without a schema ([http], [https]) is not a complete address, and a [Referer]—which would itself be a [/langue/...] address—would redirect to this action, creating a loop. In both cases, the user is redirected back to the site’s root. The cookie’s lifetime is specified by a [timedelta]: [set_cookie] accepts this just as well as a number of seconds.

    # =========================================================================
# controllers/agenda.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The calendar page: selecting a doctor and a day, that
# doctor’s schedule for that day, booking and canceling appointments.
#
#    GE T /agenda?idMedecin=1&day=2026-09-2             3 the page
#    GE T /agenda?idMedecin=1&day=2026-09-23&book=7     the same page, with
#                                                           the booking window
#                                                           for time slot 7 is open
#    POST /calendar/book                                   creates an appointment
#    POST /calendar/canc                                  el cancels an appointment
#
# The entire page is described by its URL: you can reload it, add it
# to your favorites, or use the browser’s “Back” button—without a single line
# of JavaScript.
#
# What everyone sees and can do:
#
#    | rol         e | displayed re           served slot           | Reserve | Cancel |
#   |---------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------|---------|
#    | ADMIN, DOCTOR | patient name                         | for     a patient | yes |
#                  |                                    |            | selected from list | |
#    | USER (patient)| “Reserved,” or SON name if it i s | for himself, if he| no (*) |
#                  | | his own            appointment          | does not already have an appointment| |
#                  |                                                         | | upcoming | |
#
#    (*) The patient cancels their appointment from their "My Account" page.
#
# CONFIDENTIALITÉ: for a patient, the names of the AUTRES patients are not
# simply hidden by the view—it is never included in the template
# passed to the view. The HTML sent to the browser therefore does not contain it,
# nor is it hidden (otherwise, simply “View Source” would reveal it).
#
# No reservations in the past: the “Reserve” button only appears
# for today and the following days (and the business layer would reject it
# in any case).
#
# Security: all URL /calendar operations require an authenticated user
# (see auth/securite.py: anything that isn’t @public). @roles_requis
# on an action also requires one of the listed roles. Without a valid token:
# return to /login; insufficient role: 403 page.
# =========================================================================
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date

from flask import Blueprint, abort, redirect, render_template, request, url_for

from rdvmedecins.auth.securite import roles_requis
from rdvmedecins.domain.agenda import AgendaMedecinJour
from rdvmedecins.entities import Client, Personne, Role
from rdvmedecins.metier import dates
from rdvmedecins.metier.exception import MetierException
from rdvmedecins.models.modeles_vues import (AgendaModele, AgendaVue, LigneAgendaVue, Message,
                                             OptionVue, ReservationVue)
from rdvmedecins.web import outils
from rdvmedecins.web.flash import flash_erreur, flash_succes
from rdvmedecins.web.services import application

agenda = Blueprint("agenda", __name__, url_prefix="/agenda")


# what the controller knows about the user, to determine what to display
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Droits:
    gestionnaire: bool  # ADMIN or DOCTOR
    patient: Client | None  # the logged-in client (role USER), otherwise None
    patient_peut_reserver: bool  # USER with no upcoming appointments


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /calendar
# The parameters for URL are read in raw format (request.args.get), to
# distinguish a ABSENT parameter (None) from a VIDE parameter (?idMedecin=).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@agenda.get("")
def afficher():
    erreur = None
    utilisateur = outils.utilisateur()
    droits = calculer_droits()

     # the day: the one from URL if it is valid, otherwise today
    jour = dates.aujourdhui()
    jour_brut = request.args.get("jour")
    if jour_brut is not None:
        jour_demande = outils.date_valide(jour_brut)
        if jour_demande is not None:
            jour = jour_demande
        else:
            erreur = "ERRORS.INVALID_DATE"
    jour_reservable = jour >= dates.aujourdhui()

     # the doctor: the one from URL; otherwise, for a logged-in doctor, the doctor themselves
    id_medecin_brut = request.args.get("idMedecin")
    id_medecin = outils.entier_positif(id_medecin_brut)
    if id_medecin_brut is None and utilisateur.role == Role.DOCTOR:
        medecin = application().get_medecin_by_user_id(utilisateur.user_id)
        id_medecin = medecin.id if medecin else None

     # the drop-down list of doctors
    medecins = [option(m, m.id == id_medecin) for m in application().get_all_medecins()]

     # the calendar, if a doctor is selected (and the date is valid)
    vue_agenda = None
    if id_medecin is not None and erreur is None:
        agenda_medecin = application().get_agenda_medecin_jour(id_medecin, jour)
        if agenda_medecin is None:
            erreur = "ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND"
        else:
            vue_agenda = agenda_vue(agenda_medecin, droits, jour_reservable)

     # the booking window: only if the requested time slot is
     # bookable by this user
    reservation = None
    id_creneau = outils.entier_positif(request.args.get("reserver"))
    if vue_agenda is not None and id_creneau is not None:
        ligne = next((l for l in vue_agenda.lignes if l.id_creneau == id_creneau and l.reservable),
                     None)
        if ligne is not None:
            reservation = ReservationVue(
                ligne.id_creneau,
                ligne.horaire,
                [option(c, False) for c in application().get_all_clients()]
                if droits.gestionnaire else [],
                outils.libelle(droits.patient) if droits.patient else None)

    modele = AgendaModele(
        titre_page="AGENDA.PAGE_TITLE",
        erreur=Message(erreur) if erreur else None,
        medecins=medecins,
        id_medecin=id_medecin,
        jour=outils.iso(jour),
        agenda=vue_agenda,
        reservation=reservation,
        url_retour=url_agenda(id_medecin, jour) if id_medecin is not None else url_for("agenda.afficher"),
        info=info_patient(droits, vue_agenda))
    return render_template("agenda.html", modele=modele)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /calendar/book   fields: idMedecin, day, idCreneau, idClient
#
# For a patient (USER), the field idClient is IGNORÉ: he books
# always books for himself. Trusting a field sent by the
# browser would allow a malicious patient to make a reservation in someone else’s name.
#
# "Post/Redirect/Get" pattern: regardless of the result, we do not
# generate a page here—we display a flash message and redirect
# to the calendar (see example 20).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@agenda.post("/reserver")
@roles_requis(Role.ADMIN, Role.DOCTOR, Role.USER)
def reserver():
    id_medecin, jour = lire_agenda_demande()
    id_creneau = outils.entier_positif(request.form.get("idCreneau"))
    if id_medecin is None or id_creneau is None:
        abort(400)  # -> “Invalid Request” page (see web/erreurs.py)
    utilisateur = outils.utilisateur()

    if utilisateur.est_patient:
        client = outils.patient_connecte(application())
    else:
        id_client = outils.entier_positif(request.form.get("idClient"))
        if id_client is None:
             # No patient selected: the booking window reopens
            flash_erreur("ERRORS.CHOOSE_PATIENT")
            return redirect(url_agenda(id_medecin, jour, id_creneau))
        client = application().get_client_by_id(id_client)

    creneau = application().get_creneau_by_id(id_creneau)
    if client is None:
        flash_erreur("ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND")
    elif creneau is None or creneau.id_medecin != id_medecin:
        flash_erreur("ERRORS.SLOT_NOT_FOUND")
    else:
        try:
             # the rules (not in the past, only one upcoming appointment per
             # patient, available time slot) are verified by the business logic layer
            application().ajouter_rv(jour, creneau, client)
            flash_succes("AGENDA.BOOKED")
        except MetierException as e:
             # same rule, but a message to the second person when it is the
             # patient themselves who is booking (“You already have...” rather
             # than “This patient...””). Other exceptions (true
             # errors) are not caught: 500 error.
            if e.cle == "ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT" and utilisateur.est_patient:
                flash_erreur("AGENDA.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO")
            else:
                flash_erreur(e.cle, **e.parametres)
    return redirect(url_agenda(id_medecin, jour))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /agenda/cancel    fields: idRv, idMedecin, day
# (a patient cancels SON an appointment from "My Account," not from here)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@agenda.post("/annuler")
@roles_requis(Role.ADMIN, Role.DOCTOR)
def annuler():
    id_medecin, jour = lire_agenda_demande()
    id_rv = outils.entier_positif(request.form.get("idRv"))
    if id_medecin is None or id_rv is None:
        abort(400)
    rv = application().get_rv_by_id(id_rv)
    if rv is None:
         # already canceled (by someone else, or by double-clicking)
        flash_erreur("ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND")
    else:
        application().supprimer_rv(rv)
        flash_succes("AGENDA.CANCELLED")
    return redirect(url_agenda(id_medecin, jour))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Who is logged in, and what actions are they authorized to perform on this page?
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def calculer_droits() -> Droits:
    if not outils.utilisateur().est_patient:
        return Droits(True, None, False)
    patient = outils.patient_connecte(application())
    rv_a_venir = application().get_rv_a_venir_client(patient.id)
    return Droits(False, patient, not rv_a_venir)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# The doctor’s schedule, formatted for viewing—and filtered according to permissions
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def agenda_vue(agenda_medecin: AgendaMedecinJour, droits: Droits, jour_reservable: bool) -> AgendaVue:
    id_medecin = agenda_medecin.medecin.id
    jour = agenda_medecin.jour
    lignes = []
    for cmj in agenda_medecin.creneaux_medecin_jour:
        creneau, rv = cmj.creneau, cmj.rv
        libre = rv is None
         # the logged-in patient’s appointment?
        moi = rv is not None and droits.patient is not None and rv.id_client == droits.patient.id
        lignes.append(LigneAgendaVue(
            id_creneau=creneau.id,
            horaire=outils.horaire(creneau),
            libre=libre,
             # LE privacy setting: a patient only sees the name
             # for the SON appointment; for others, None (the view displays “Reserved”)
            patient=outils.libelle(rv.client) if rv is not None and (droits.gestionnaire or moi) else None,
            moi=moi,
            reservable=libre and jour_reservable and (droits.gestionnaire or droits.patient_peut_reserver),
            url_reserver=url_agenda(id_medecin, jour, creneau.id),
            id_rv=rv.id if rv is not None and droits.gestionnaire else None))
    return AgendaVue(outils.libelle(agenda_medecin.medecin), outils.formater_jour(jour), lignes)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- Utility functions

# hidden fields idMedecin / day in the forms POST; (None, None) if they are invalid
def lire_agenda_demande() -> tuple[int | None, date | None]:
    id_medecin = outils.entier_positif(request.form.get("idMedecin"))
    jour = outils.date_valide(request.form.get("jour"))
    return (None, None) if id_medecin is None or jour is None else (id_medecin, jour)


# /calendar?idMedecin=1&day=2026-09-23[&reserver=7]: url_for appends to the end of
# the URL parameters that are not path variables
def url_agenda(id_medecin: int, jour: date, reserver: int | None = None) -> str:
    if reserver is None:
        return url_for("agenda.afficher", idMedecin=id_medecin, jour=outils.iso(jour))
    return url_for("agenda.afficher", idMedecin=id_medecin, jour=outils.iso(jour), reserver=reserver)


def option(p: Personne, selectionne: bool) -> OptionVue:
    return OptionVue(p.id, outils.libelle(p), selectionne)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# the informational message for a patient who already has an upcoming appointment
# (which is why there is no “Book” button), or None. Not needed if SON
# the appointment appears in the displayed calendar (in blue): this is the case
# after they’ve just scheduled it, in which case the message would be moved.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def info_patient(droits: Droits, vue: AgendaVue | None) -> str | None:
    if droits.patient is None or droits.patient_peut_reserver:
        return None
    rv_affiche = vue is not None and any(ligne.moi for ligne in vue.lignes)
    return None if rv_affiche else "AGENDA.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO"

    11.16.2.1. The URL for the page

    The entire page is described by its URL: [/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2026-09-26] displays Doctor #1’s schedule for that day; [&reserver=4] also opens the booking window for slot #4. The appointment booking window is therefore not opened by [JavaScript]: the server generates a page containing the window. This means you can reload the page, bookmark it, use the browser’s “Back” button, and the application works without [JavaScript] (the application’s only script is used for confirmation windows, and it works without it as well; see example 21).

    11.16.2.2. GET /agenda

    • lines 65–68: what the action knows about the user to determine the display: a “manager” (ADMIN or DOCTOR) or a patient, who may or may not make a reservation;
    • lines 83–91: the day: the day specified by URL if it is valid; otherwise, today. Parameters are read in raw format ([request.args.get]) to distinguish between a missing parameter ([None]: the default value is used, with no error) and an invalid parameter (an error is reported). Only today and the following days are bookable;
    • lines 94–98: the doctor: the one from URL; otherwise, for a logged-in doctor, the doctor themselves: a doctor can view their daily schedule directly upon logging in;
    • line 101: the drop-down list of doctors, read from the cache, with the selected doctor highlighted;
    • lines 104–110: the schedule, if a doctor is selected and the date is valid. A nonexistent doctor (an ID manually modified in URL) triggers an error message, not an error page;
    • lines 114–125: the booking window, only if the requested time slot exists and is bookable by this user: a patient who adds [&reserver=2] to URL for a time slot that is already booked will see nothing. [next(...)] searches for the corresponding calendar entry (example 21). The window displays a list of patients to an administrator; for each patient, it displays their own name;
    • Lines 127–137: The page template. [url_retour] is the URL for the calendar without the booking window; the "Cancel" button in the window takes you there.

    11.16.2.3. POST /calendar/reserve

    • line 152: All roles can make reservations. The decorator documents the rule and protects it in case a fourth role were to appear in the future;
    • lines 154–157: the form’s hidden fields. Invalid fields can only result from a manually crafted request: error 400;
    • lines 160–168: the patient for the appointment. For a patient, it is always the patient themselves: the field [idClient] is ignored. Trusting a field sent by the browser would allow a patient to book on behalf of another. For an administrator who has not selected a patient, the booking window reopens with a message;
    • lines 170–189: validations (the patient exists, the time slot exists and belongs to the doctor in the calendar), followed by the booking. Business rules are verified by the business logic layer; a [MetierException] becomes a flash error message. The message “only one upcoming appointment” is adapted when the patient makes the booking themselves (“You already have...” rather than “This patient already has...”);
    • line 190: in all cases, return to the calendar (schema PRG).

    11.16.2.4. POST /calendar/cancel

    • Lines 197–211: Canceling an appointment, reserved for administrators (a patient cancels their appointment from their account). An appointment that has already been canceled (by someone else or by double-clicking) displays a message, not an error.

    11.16.2.5. Permissions, the formatted calendar, and utility functions

    • lines 217–222: user permissions. For a patient, it is necessary to view their upcoming appointments: an empty list is “incorrect,” hence [not rv_a_venir];
    • lines 228–248: the domain’s calendar, formatted for display and filtered according to permissions. This is where patient confidentiality comes into play (line 243): for a patient, the names of other patients are not merely hidden from view; they are never included in the template. The HTML sent to the browser therefore does not contain it, even if hidden (otherwise, a simple “View Source” would reveal it). The “Reserve” button appears only when there is an available time slot, a bookable day, and a user with the right to make a reservation; the “Cancel” button appears only for an administrator;
    • lines 254–257: the hidden fields [idMedecin] and [jour] in the POST forms, validated;
    • lines 262–265: the URL from the calendar. [url_for] adds the named parameters that are not path variables to URL as parameters (example 16);
    • lines 278–282: the informational message for a patient who already has an upcoming appointment: it explains why the “Book” buttons are missing. It is not displayed if the patient’s own appointment appears in the calendar (in blue), which is the case immediately after booking. [any(...)] returns [True] if either condition is true.

    11.16.3. controllers/personnes.py

    The management of doctors and clients, reserved for the administrator, is identical: same list, same form, same rules. Rather than writing the same actions twice, we write them once, in a blueprint factory.

    # =========================================================================
# controllers/personnes.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The management of doctors and clients (reserved for ADMIN) are
# IDENTIQUES: same list, same form, same rules. Rather than
# writing the same actions twice, they are written once in a
# FABRIQUE DE BLUEPRINTS: the function creer_blueprint builds a
# complete blueprint from a "configuration" that specifies which QUOI to call and
# and QUELS labels to display. controllers/medecins.py and controllers/clients.py
# each calls the other using its own identifier. This results in the following for each:
#
#    GE T /doctor                  s list
#    GE T /doctors/add            empty form
#    POST /doctors/add            create
#    GE T /doctors/<id>/edit      pre-filled form
#    POST /doctors/<id>/edit      edit
#    POST /doctors/<id>/delete     deletion
#
# (and the corresponding URL under /clients). The views are also shared:
# templates/people/liste.html and templates/people/formulaire.html.
#
# SÉCURITÉ: a before_request DU BLUEPRINT requires the role ADMIN. It
# runs before the CHAQUE blueprint action—including those that are
# would add later: the rule is written once and for all.
# =========================================================================
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass

from flask import Blueprint, abort, redirect, render_template, url_for

from rdvmedecins.auth.securite import exiger_roles
from rdvmedecins.entities import Personne, Role
from rdvmedecins.forms.formulaires import FormulairePersonne
from rdvmedecins.metier.donnees import DonneesPersonne
from rdvmedecins.metier.exception import MetierException
from rdvmedecins.models.modeles_vues import (ClesPersonnes, EtatFormulaire, FormulairePersonneModele,
                                             ListePersonnesModele, Message, PersonneVue,
                                             ValeursPersonne)
from rdvmedecins.web import validation
from rdvmedecins.web.flash import flash_erreur, flash_succes


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# what each type of person must provide. The last five fields
# are FONCTIONS: medecins.py and clients.py store lambdas in them that
# call methods of the ApplicationModel (get_all_medecins...).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ConfigPersonnes:
    nom: str  # "doctors" or "clients": the name of the blueprint, and the beginning of the URL
    cles: ClesPersonnes
    lister: Callable[[], list[Personne]]  # () -> list
    trouver: Callable[[int], Personne | None]  # id -> person
    ajouter: Callable[[DonneesPersonne], Personne]  # data -> person created
    modifier: Callable[[int, DonneesPersonne], Personne]  # (id, data) -> person modified
    supprimer: Callable[[int], None]  # id -> nothing


def creer_blueprint(config: ConfigPersonnes) -> Blueprint:
    bp = Blueprint(config.nom, __name__, url_prefix=f"/{config.nom}")

     # the URL of an action from the CE blueprint: url("list") -> "/doctors"
    def url(action: str, **parametres) -> str:
        return url_for(f"{config.nom}.{action}", **parametres)

     # All actions in the blueprint are reserved for ADMIN
    @bp.before_request
    def reserve_admin():
        exiger_roles(Role.ADMIN)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     # GET /doctors (or /clients)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.get("")
    def liste():
        personnes = [PersonneVue(p.titre, p.prenom, p.nom, login(p),
                                 url("formulaire_modification", id=p.id),
                                 url("supprimer", id=p.id))
                     for p in config.lister()]
        modele = ListePersonnesModele(config.cles.titre, None, config.cles, url("formulaire_ajout"),
                                      personnes)
        return render_template("personnes/liste.html", modele=modele)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     # GET /doctors/add
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.get("/ajouter")
    def formulaire_ajout():
        return afficher_formulaire(None, ValeursPersonne(), {}, None, None)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     # POST /doctors/add
     # FormulairePersonne() reads the input; validate() checks it.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.post("/ajouter")
    def ajouter():
        form = FormulairePersonne()
        if not form.validate():
            return afficher_formulaire(None, valeurs_saisies(form), validation.erreurs_de(form),
                                       None, None)
        try:
            personne = config.ajouter(donnees(form))
        except MetierException as e:
            return afficher_erreur_metier(None, valeurs_saisies(form), e)
        flash_succes(config.cles.ajoute, **parametres(personne))
        return redirect(url("liste"))

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     # GET /doctors/<id>/edit
     # <int:id>: The ID must consist of numbers - /doctors/abc/edit does not
     # matches any URL (404 page)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.get("/<int:id>/modifier")
    def formulaire_modification(id: int):
        personne = config.trouver(id)
        if personne is None:
            abort(404)
        valeurs = ValeursPersonne(personne.titre, personne.prenom, personne.nom, login(personne),
                                  personne.version)
        return afficher_formulaire(id, valeurs, {}, None, None)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     # POST /doctors/<id>/edit
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.post("/<int:id>/modifier")
    def modifier(id: int):
        form = FormulairePersonne()
        if not form.validate():
            return afficher_formulaire(id, valeurs_saisies(form), validation.erreurs_de(form),
                                       None, None)
        try:
            personne = config.modifier(id, donnees(form))
        except MetierException as e:
            return afficher_erreur_metier(id, valeurs_saisies(form), e)
        flash_succes(config.cles.modifie, **parametres(personne))
        return redirect(url("liste"))

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     # POST /doctors/<id>/delete
     # (A confirmation prompt asking "Are you sure?" appears before the
     # form; see static/js/app.js)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.post("/<int:id>/supprimer")
    def supprimer(id: int):
        personne = config.trouver(id)
        try:
            config.supprimer(id)
            flash_succes(config.cles.supprime, **parametres(personne))
        except MetierException as e:
            flash_erreur(e.cle, **e.parametres)
        return redirect(url("liste"))

     # ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions

     # id None: creation form; otherwise: update form.
     # errors: field -> message key; error: the key of the bottom
     # autres_champs: fields to be highlighted in red as well
    def afficher_formulaire(id: int | None, valeurs: ValeursPersonne, erreurs: dict[str, str],
                            erreur: str | None, autres_champs: list[str] | None):
        creation = id is None
        etat: EtatFormulaire = validation.etat(erreurs, autres_champs)
        modele = FormulairePersonneModele(
            titre_page=config.cles.ajouter if creation else config.cles.modifier,
            erreur=validation.message_page(erreurs, Message(erreur) if erreur else None),
            valeurs=valeurs,
            etat=etat,
            creation=creation,
            action=url("ajouter") if creation else url("modifier", id=id),
            url_liste=url("liste"))
        return render_template("personnes/formulaire.html", modele=modele)

     # a business rule rejected the write operation: the form is redisplayed,
     # with the user’s input and the business-layer message
    def afficher_erreur_metier(id: int | None, valeurs: ValeursPersonne, e: MetierException):
        if e.cle in ("ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND", "ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND"):
             # which has since been deleted by another ADMIN: return to the list
            flash_erreur(e.cle)
            return redirect(url("liste"))
         # the message moves to the bottom of the page; the relevant fields, if any, are
         # highlighted in red so the user can immediately see what to correct
        return afficher_formulaire(id, valeurs, {}, e.cle, validation.CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER.get(e.cle))

    return bp


# what the user entered (excluding the password: it is never sent
# to the browser). form.<field>.data: the value, after filters
def valeurs_saisies(form: FormulairePersonne) -> ValeursPersonne:
    return ValeursPersonne(form.titre.data or "", form.prenom.data or "", form.nom.data or "",
                           form.login.data or "", form.version.data)


# the validated form -> the data expected by the business layer
def donnees(form: FormulairePersonne) -> DonneesPersonne:
    return DonneesPersonne(form.titre.data, form.nom.data, form.prenom.data, form.login.data,
                           form.password.data, form.version.data)


# {name} and {login} for the "added / modified / deleted" messages
def parametres(personne: Personne | None) -> dict[str, str]:
    if personne is None:
        return {"nom": "", "login": ""}
    return {"nom": f"{personne.prenom} {personne.nom}", "login": login(personne)}


def login(personne: Personne) -> str:
    return personne.user.login if personne.user else ""
    • lines 49–56: what each type of entity must provide: the blueprint name (which is also the beginning of URL), the translation keys, and five functions: list, find, add, edit, and delete. This is the same process as for business layer descriptors;
    • Lines 59–60: The factory creates a blueprint, whose name and the prefix of URL come from the configuration. The actions are internal functions of [creer_blueprint]: they have access to the factory’s variable [config]. Each call to [creer_blueprint] creates a new blueprint, with its own actions;
    • lines 63–64: the URL for an action in this blueprint: [url("liste")] returns [/medecins] for the doctors’ blueprint and [/clients] for the clients’ blueprint;
    • lines 67–69: a blueprint [before_request]: it runs before every action in the blueprint (and only in this one), after those of the application. All actions are thus reserved for the administrator, including any that might be added later: the rule is written once and applies to all;
    • lines 74–82: the list. [@bp.get("")]: the route is the prefix of the blueprint itself ([/medecins]);
    • lines 95–106: the add operation: form validation (input errors, displayed below the fields), call to the business layer (business errors, displayed at the bottom of the page), followed by a flash message and redirection to the list. The flash messages receive parameters: the person’s name and login;
    • lines 113–120: the edit form, pre-filled with the record’s version (optimistic locking). A nonexistent person results in a 404 page;
    • lines 125–136: the update, modeled after the add operation;
    • lines 143–151: the delete operation, confirmed beforehand by the confirmation window (example 21). A rejection by the business layer (a doctor who has appointments) results in a flash error message;
    • lines 158–170: the add form ([id] equals [None]) or edit form, along with its status (values, errors, fields highlighted in red);
    • lines 174–181: a business error: a person who has since been deleted by another administrator is returned to the list; the others redisplay the form, with the relevant fields highlighted in red;
    • lines 188–190: the values to be redisplayed: what the user entered, never the password;
    • lines 194–196: the validated form, converted into data for the business layer;
    • lines 200–203: the parameters for the “added/modified/deleted” messages.

    # =========================================================================
# controllers/medecins.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Physician management (ADMIN role only). All actions are
# generated by controllers/personnes.py: all that remains here is to call QUOI
# to call and QUELS to display labels.
#
# The configuration functions are LAMBDAS (functions without
# a name, written on the spot): application() is called only when
# the action is executed, during a request—the ApplicationModel does not exist
# when this module is imported.
# =========================================================================
from rdvmedecins.controllers.personnes import ConfigPersonnes, creer_blueprint
from rdvmedecins.models.modeles_vues import ClesPersonnes
from rdvmedecins.web.services import application

medecins = creer_blueprint(ConfigPersonnes(
    nom="medecins",
    cles=ClesPersonnes(
        titre="MEDECINS.TITLE",
        ajouter="MEDECINS.ADD",
        modifier="MEDECINS.EDIT",
        vide="MEDECINS.EMPTY",
        confirmer_suppression="MEDECINS.DELETE_CONFIRM",
        ajoute="MEDECINS.ADDED",
        modifie="MEDECINS.UPDATED",
        supprime="MEDECINS.DELETED"),
    lister=lambda: application().get_all_medecins(),
    trouver=lambda id: application().get_medecin_by_id(id),
    ajouter=lambda donnees: application().ajouter_medecin(donnees),
    modifier=lambda id, donnees: application().modifier_medecin(id, donnees),
    supprimer=lambda id: application().supprimer_medecin(id)))

    The doctors’ blueprint, generated by [creer_blueprint] along with its configuration. The configuration functions are anonymous functions ([lambda]), which call [ApplicationModel]. Why not write [lister=application().get_all_medecins] directly? Because this module is executed when it is imported, at startup, before the application is created: [application()], which requires [current_app], would fail. The anonymous function defers the call until the action is executed, during a request.

    # =========================================================================
# controllers/inscription.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# "Create a customer account": a patient who does not yet have an account
# creates one themselves. Routes PUBLIQUES (we don’t have an account yet, per
# definition):
#
#    POST /registration/log  in "Create a customer account" button on the
#                              authentication page: verifies the captcha from
#                              CETTE page, then opens the form
#    GE T /registrat        ion the form
#    POST /registrati        on the registration process, then returns to the login page
#
# The process is protected against bots by the UN CAPTCHA on the
# authentication page:
#    1. The "Create a Customer Account" button sends the login form
#       to /registration/access; if the CAPTCHA is entered correctly, the server
#       issues a token (see auth/passe_inscription.py);
#    2. Without a valid pass, /registration redirects to the
#       authentication page—typing URL directly does nothing;
#    3. The pass is used up upon creation: a solved CAPTCHA
#       allows you to create UN an account;
#    4. Additionally, the number of accounts created per hour per IP address is
#       limited (see auth/limiteur.py).
#
# The account created is exactly the one that ADMIN would create from the
# "Clients" page (same business-layer method: ajouter_client), if this
# is simply the patient CHOISIT entering their login and password (required,
# with confirmation).
# =========================================================================
from flask import Blueprint, current_app, redirect, render_template, request, url_for

from rdvmedecins.auth import passe_inscription
from rdvmedecins.auth.securite import publique
from rdvmedecins.controllers.auth import adresse_ip
from rdvmedecins.forms.formulaires import FormulaireInscription
from rdvmedecins.metier.donnees import DonneesPersonne
from rdvmedecins.metier.exception import MetierException
from rdvmedecins.models.modeles_vues import InscriptionModele, Message, ValeursPersonne
from rdvmedecins.web import validation
from rdvmedecins.web.flash import flash_erreur, flash_succes
from rdvmedecins.web.services import application, captchas, limiteur, passes

inscription = Blueprint("inscription", __name__, url_prefix="/inscription")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /registration/acces  s fields: captchaId, captcha (those on the
# authentication page; username and password, which are also sent, are ignored)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@inscription.post("/acces")
@publique
def acces():
    ip = adresse_ip()

     # too many accounts created recently from this address: no need to proceed further
    minutes = limiteur().minutes_blocage_inscription(ip)
    if minutes > 0:
        flash_erreur("ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS", minutes=str(minutes))
        return redirect(url_for("auth.afficher_login"))

     # captcha missing or incorrect: return to the authentication page, with
     # a new image (one failure counts as a failed login attempt)
    if not captchas().verifier(request.form.get("captchaId"), request.form.get("captcha")):
        limiteur().echec_login(ip, "")
        flash_erreur("ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT")
        return redirect(url_for("auth.afficher_login"))

     # Correct CAPTCHA: Grant access and open the form
    reponse = redirect(url_for("inscription.formulaire"))
    passe_inscription.deposer_cookie(reponse, passes().emettre(), current_app.config["COOKIE_SECURE"])
    return reponse


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@inscription.get("")
@publique
def formulaire():
    if not passes().est_valide(request.cookies.get(passe_inscription.COOKIE)):
        return retour_login()
    return afficher(ValeursPersonne(), {}, None, None)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@inscription.post("")
@publique
def creer():
    passe = request.cookies.get(passe_inscription.COOKIE)
    if not passes().est_valide(passe):
        return retour_login()
    ip = adresse_ip()
    form = FormulaireInscription()
    form.validate()
    valeurs = ValeursPersonne(form.titre.data or "Mr", form.prenom.data or "",
                              form.nom.data or "", form.login.data or "", None)

     # 1. Have too many accounts been created recently from this address?
    minutes = limiteur().minutes_blocage_inscription(ip)
    if minutes > 0:
        return afficher(valeurs, {}, Message("ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS", {"minutes": str(minutes)}),
                        None)

     # 2. All data entry errors at once (fields + confirmation):
         # the user corrects them all at once
    erreurs = validation.erreurs_de(form)
    if "password" not in erreurs and "confirmation" not in erreurs \
            and form.password.data != form.confirmation.data:
        erreurs["confirmation"] = "ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER"
    if erreurs:
        return afficher(valeurs, erreurs, None, None)

     # 3. Account creation (customer + account USER, in a single transaction)
    try:
        application().ajouter_client(DonneesPersonne(form.titre.data, form.nom.data,
                                                     form.prenom.data, form.login.data,
                                                     form.password.data))
    except MetierException as e:
         # Username or first name + last name already taken: the pass remains valid
        return afficher(valeurs, {}, Message(e.cle), validation.CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER.get(e.cle))

     # 4. The passcode has been used: it will not allow the creation of a second account
    passes().consommer(passe)
    limiteur().inscription_reussie(ip)

     # 5. Return to the login page; login credentials are pre-filled
    flash_succes("INSCRIPTION.DONE", login=form.login.data)
    reponse = redirect(url_for("auth.afficher_login", login=form.login.data))
    passe_inscription.effacer_cookie(reponse)
    return reponse


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions

# No valid token: return to the authentication page
def retour_login():
    flash_erreur("ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT")
    return redirect(url_for("auth.afficher_login"))


# the form; the password is never sent back to the browser
def afficher(valeurs: ValeursPersonne, erreurs: dict[str, str], erreur: Message | None,
             autres_champs: list[str] | None):
    modele = InscriptionModele("INSCRIPTION.TITLE", validation.message_page(erreurs, erreur),
                               valeurs, validation.etat(erreurs, autres_champs))
    return render_template("inscription.html", modele=modele)
    • Lines 51–72: The “Create a Customer Account” button on the login page submits the login form to this action (using the [formaction] attribute, Example 20). It checks the limit on account creations, then the CAPTCHA on the login page; if it is correct, it issues a token ([auth/passe_inscription.py]) and redirects to the registration form. A failure is counted as a failed login attempt (with an empty username);
    • lines 78–83: the form, only with a valid passcode: typing the address [/inscription] directly redirects to the login page;
    • lines 89–133: account creation: - the passcode, again; - [form.validate()] is called, but its result is ignored: we want all input errors at once, including any mismatch between the password and its confirmation, which is then verified by the action (provided both fields are otherwise valid). The user corrects them all at once; - the client and their account are created using the same business-logic method as for the administrator; - the pass is consumed, and the creation is counted by the limiter; - return to the login page, with a message and the login pre-filled (parameter [login] from URL). The pass cookie is cleared.
